---
title: "Unified Report Model"
---

SCGSim is an independent downstream toolkit, not official gsim. It provides
strict solver-specific resolvers and a consistent, trust-first notebook reading
surface without pretending different physical quantities are identical.

## Common envelope

Current Palace `show_all_results()` presentation follows this order:

1. run trustworthiness, run identity, and receipt state;
2. numerical evidence and simulation cost/resource benchmarks;
3. available solver-specific physics.

`inspect_run_trustworthiness()` supports completed, failed, and partial returned
packages. It preserves the recorded receipt status and may expose the latest
readable evidence without promoting an incomplete run. The strict
`resolve_palace_result(..., expected_handoff_id=...)` path accepts only a
completed package whose handoff, receipt, solver, and artifact hashes validate.

## Honesty rule

Solver-specific quantities remain solver-specific. Electrostatic matrices,
eigenfrequencies, driven network responses, field-energy participation, Q3D
matrices, and Q2D per-unit-length results must retain their own units,
extraction authority, and failure meaning.

For Palace, `LossTan=0.0` is also the backend-compatible config value when no
loss tangent was supplied. It does not turn an unknown assumption into a known
zero: the v2 index and detached `PalaceEprResult` retain `loss_tangent=None`,
and SCGSim leaves the corresponding inverse-Q contribution unavailable. An
explicit known zero instead gives a zero contribution. Neither state creates a
surface-loss lifetime claim. The [Eigenmode and Offline EPR guide](eigenmode-epr.qmd)
documents its analysis methods and assumptions. Palace's generic `domain-E.csv`
Volume Energy table still has no general-purpose report renderer.

## Eigenmode EPR presentation

AEDT and Palace keep separate `show_epr()` inputs and return a Plotly `Figure`;
the view consumes an existing result and does not resolve files or start a
solver. This page owns the report's visible availability and coverage contract.

Each figure separates surface and bulk participation. AEDT shows junction
inductive and capacitive participation together on a junction axis; Palace
shows its signed native port participation separately. Surface bars identify the
semantic owner or owners, interface, and baseline or requested-margin
evaluation. Hover data retains source members, field side, and loss assumptions.
The coverage annotation counts reported surface rows and source bindings or
surfaces, bulk domains, and junctions or ports.

An AEDT `ResolvedRun` provides `epr_result()` for its bound EPR record and
`show_all_results(show_details=False)` for the integrated run view; the latter
returns `None`. The view uses all requested modes at the actual last completed
pass and includes the adaptive history. Missing or partial values remain
unavailable; presentation does not fall back to an earlier complete pass. It
checks consumed result CSVs and benchmark data against hashes captured during
resolution, without consulting a live simulation object or rereading native
AEDT state. See the
[AEDT runtime reference](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd) for strict resolution and
missing-artifact behavior.

The displayed inverse-Q subtotal includes only known, unmasked baseline
surface terms. Unknown baseline losses are counted as unknown; requested mask
margins are alternative views and are not added to the subtotal. Sidewall
energy remains labeled uncomputed where it was not evaluated. These figures
show the available evidence and do not claim total device loss or a lifetime.

Palace and AEDT quantities resolved from original run packages remain bound to
their applicable receipt, artifact-hash, handoff, and solver identities. A
detached Palace EPR result retains original artifact identity and hash
references, but those references do not authenticate the detached JSON itself.
Presentation does not weaken source bindings and makes no
numerical-convergence or cross-solver-agreement claim.

The separate [Tetrahedral Mesh Quality](mesh-quality.qmd) report is bound to a
single MSH file read. Its volume, orientation, and condition evidence are
geometry diagnostics, not solver results, and do not create a hidden quality
threshold or convergence claim.

## Multi-margin Surface EPR reading surface

The existing inspection and strict-resolution split also governs native
multi-margin Surface EPR. `inspect_run_trustworthiness()` may inspect a
completed, failed, or partial package and marks unavailable mask data as
unavailable without changing the receipt state. A missing or unreadable mask
pair makes that source's masked snapshot unavailable while a valid baseline
snapshot remains readable. A strict completed resolution of a run that
requested masks requires the sealed `surface-mask-Q.csv` and
`surface-mask-energy.csv` files from the same required result source. Missing
mask files prevent strict resolution, and an existing receipt or artifact
SHA-256 mismatch remains fatal.

`PhysicsQuantitiesReport.snapshots` remains the baseline-only surface. The
typed `PhysicsQuantitiesReport.masked_snapshots` surface exposes complete
snapshots for the requested masks while preserving interface identity, margin
value and ordinal, mode or excitation, refinement pass, native index, and
source identity. Duplicate requested margins therefore remain separately
traceable; they are not duplicate contributions to a loss total.

`show_physics_quantities()` presents the latest masked participation versus
margin for each mode or excitation and exact interface, using the native
surface traces. Run trustworthiness remains the authority for AMR history and
evidence; the physics presentation does not reinterpret refinement evidence.

A native zero participation or surface energy means only that the native
contribution is zero. Without supporting geometry evidence, it does not prove
that a region was geometrically fully excluded. An unavailable inverse-Q
contribution caused by unknown loss remains unavailable rather than being
converted into a lifetime claim; participation and energy evidence stay
visible.

This report surface remains **CONVERGING** and does not add a cumulative
disjoint edge-band interpretation, portable export format, or scientific
acceptance claim.

## Current Palace scope

The support derived from upstream gsim #61 is limited to Domain Energy,
MA/MS/SA Surface EPR, exact index mapping, and Electrostatic/Eigenmode reports.
SCGSim does not implement the upstream #171 cumulative inset-band presentation.
Palace Driven and Magnetostatic implementation/reports, a Volume Energy
renderer, and a portable report snapshot/export API are outside this current
contract.
